name: agents-kanban
description: A kanban board your coding agents run themselves — each task in its own git worktree. Powered by Claude Code.

commands.title: Agents Kanban: Initialise Board In This Repo
Agents Kanban: Test Model Provider Connection

agentsKanban.worktreeRoot.markdownDescription: Where to create agent worktrees. A relative path resolves against the repository root. Empty means `.agentskanban/worktrees` inside the repository, which is added to `.gitignore` automatically. Point it outside the repository and nothing is written to your `.gitignore`.

enumDescriptions: Hide the panel and the secondary side bar while the board is in front, and restore them when you switch away.
Use VS Code's Zen Mode, which also hides the activity and status bars.
agentsKanban.focusMode.description: How much of the window the board takes while it is in front. The primary side bar is never touched — it is how you get back.

agentsKanban.sideBarHome.description: Which view the left side bar is handed back to after you press the Kanban icon. VS Code answers a click on an activity-bar icon by showing that extension's view, and offers no way to decline; this is what puts yours back. Any 'workbench.view.*' command id works — workbench.view.explorer, workbench.view.scm, workbench.view.search, workbench.view.extension.<id>. Leave it empty to let the side bar stay on the Kanban control instead.

agentsKanban.closeOnClickAway.description: Close the board when you click away from it — open a file, switch to another tab — putting the terminal and the right-hand chat back. Turn this off to make the board a pure toggle that only the icon, Ctrl+Alt+K or its tab's X can close, which is what you want if you like to glance at a file and come straight back.

agentsKanban.maxConcurrentAgents.description: How many agent sessions may run at once.

agentsKanban.permissionMode.description: Permission mode for agent sessions. Agents run in isolated worktrees, so acceptEdits is a reasonable default.

agentsKanban.notifyOnReview.description: Show a notification when an agent moves its card into a review column — its way of saying the work is ready for you to test.

agentsKanban.claudeExecutable.description: Path to the `claude` executable. Leave empty to auto-detect (PATH, then the usual install locations).

agentsKanban.statusBar.description: Show an Agents Kanban item in the status bar. A second way in, alongside the activity-bar icon and Ctrl+Alt+K, and the one that shows how many agents are running.

agentsKanban.runCommand.markdownDescription: Shell command that starts the app, run inside the session's worktree. Leave empty to detect it — a per-worktree launcher (`wt`) is preferred, then Laravel, then a `package.json` script. `${worktree}` is replaced with the worktree's path.

agentsKanban.runUrl.markdownDescription: URL to open once `agentsKanban.runCommand` is serving, e.g. `http://localhost:3000`. Leave empty to use the port the detected launcher assigned. Only used alongside a custom `runCommand`.

agentsKanban.provider.markdownDescription: Id of the provider profile agent sessions run on, from `#agentsKanban.providers#`. The default, `inherit`, changes nothing: the `claude` CLI resolves its own provider from the environment, so an existing Bedrock or gateway setup keeps working. Switch it from the board's provider picker, or with **Agents Kanban: Select Model Provider**.

agentsKanban.providers.markdownDescription: Model backends agent sessions can run on. Each profile compiles to environment variables on the `claude` process — the same variables the CLI documents — so anything Claude Code supports works here. **Credentials are never stored in settings**: they live in VS Code's secret storage, and `hasCredential` only records that one is set. Use **Agents Kanban: Add Model Provider** rather than editing this by hand. See [docs/PROVIDERS.md](https://github.com/Smile1294/Agents-Kanban/blob/main/docs/PROVIDERS.md).

id.description: Stable id. Referenced by agentsKanban.provider and used as the secret-storage key.

enumDescriptions: Change nothing — the CLI resolves its own provider from the environment.
Anthropic's API: your Claude subscription, or a Console API key.
Amazon Bedrock, through the AWS SDK credential chain.
Google Cloud's Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI).
Claude Platform on AWS, billed through AWS Marketplace.
Anything serving the Anthropic Messages API at a URL: an LLM gateway, a self-hosted proxy, or a local model behind a translation proxy.

baseUrl.description: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL for a gateway; the per-provider endpoint override otherwise.

resource.description: Microsoft Foundry resource name, when baseUrl is not given.

region.description: AWS_REGION for Bedrock, CLOUD_ML_REGION for Vertex.

regionPrefix.description: ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX — which cross-region inference profile prefix to try first.

workspaceId.description: ANTHROPIC_AWS_WORKSPACE_ID, for Claude Platform on AWS.

enumDescriptions: Send the credential as Authorization: Bearer (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN). The default, and what most gateways want.
authStyle.description: Which header the credential goes in. The wrong one reaches the gateway in a header it does not read, and returns 401.

hasCredential.description: Set automatically when a credential is stored in secret storage. Not the credential itself.

credentialFromEnv.description: Read the credential from this environment variable instead of secret storage.

headers.description: Extra request headers, sent as ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS.

gatewayAuth.description: The gateway authenticates upstream itself, so the CLI sends no SigV4 signature or key of its own (CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_*_AUTH).

disableBetas.description: Stop sending Anthropic's experimental anthropic-beta header values. The documented fix for 'Unexpected value(s) for the anthropic-beta header', which most translation proxies return.

disableNonessentialTraffic.description: Set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1, as the gateway documentation advises.

models.description: Model ids to offer in the picker instead of the built-in Claude ones. Needed off first-party: Bedrock wants us.anthropic.claude-opus-5, and a router serving another model needs its own id.

contextWindow.description: Context window for this profile's models, so the context meter has a denominator when the model is not one we know.

env.description: Extra environment variables, applied last. The escape hatch for anything not covered above.

agentsKanban.discoverModels.markdownDescription: Ask the `claude` CLI which models it can actually run, instead of using a built-in list. This is what puts newly released models — and the ones your provider serves — in the picker without waiting for an extension update, and it is where the per-model effort levels and extended-thinking support come from. The answer is cached per provider; refresh it with **Agents Kanban: Refresh Model List**. Turn this off to use the built-in list only.
